newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Coffee prices near record at Tanzania auctions.
newsitem.headline: Coffee prices near record at Tanzania auctions.

text.p: Tanzania's premium grade mild-washed Arabica coffees have been reaching near record prices at auctions in the northern Tanzanian coffee town of Moshi, a senior industry official said on Thursday.

"We've never had such high prices in 22 months. They've been moving up all along -- in some cases by big margins," Edward Sannda, managing director of the state-run Tanzania Coffee Board (TCB), told Reuters.

Sannda, speaking in a telephone interview from the TCB's headquarters in Moshi, said bags of A and AA grades had been fetching $200 or more per 60-kg bag at auction. Tanzania holds coffee auctions twice a month in Moshi.
That price compared to around half that three months ago.
Independent coffee traders put the average price of top grade northern coffees at $180 per bag at the last auction compared to $110 at the beginning of January.
Sannda said the increases started around January.

Asked what factors had caused the price increase, Sannda cited a surprise decline in arabica output from Brazil and industrial strife in Colombia's main port at Cartagena which had hit export coffee shipments.
"A lot of consumer countries had expected production from Brazil to be very high, but their production was much lower than people thought," he said.
Industry experts added that tight supply because of drought in most of East Africa had also helped prices higher.
